claims.claim: The House can force floor consideration via a discharge motion signed by a majority of the House
claims.sourceSpan: was construed to mean 218 Members

claims.claim: By a discharge motion, which becomes eligible for a vote once a majority of the House â€” 218 members â€” has signed it
claims.sourceSpan: A motion to discharge that has been on the calendar for at least seven legislative days (except during the last six days of a session of Congress) shall be privileged only at a time or place, designated by the Speaker, in the legislative schedule within two legislative days after the day on which a Member whose signature appears thereon announces to the House an intention to offer the motion.
claims.note: Pass 1 finding. Signing by 218 Members does not immediately make the motion 'eligible for a vote' â€” it enters the motion on the Calendar of Motions to Discharge Committees, and clause 2(c)(1) requires a further seven-legislative-day layover plus a signatory Member's announcement of intent before privileged call-up. Simplified to 'By a discharge motion signed by a majority of the House.'

claims.sourceSpan: The House shall divide after the Speaker has put a question to a vote by voice as provided in clause 6 of rule I if the Speaker is in doubt or division is demanded. Those in favor of the question shall first rise or otherwise indicate from their seats and be counted, and then those opposed.

claims.claim: Verbatim quote of Rule XX clause 1(b), including the 'unless the Speaker invokes another procedure' qualifier
claims.sourceSpan: If a Member, Delegate, or Resident Commissioner requests a recorded vote, and that request is supported by at least one-fifth of a quorum, the vote shall be taken by electronic device unless the Speaker invokes another procedure for recording votes provided in this rule.

claims.claim: Clause 1(b) adds: 'If a Member, Delegate, or Resident Commissioner requests a recorded vote, and that request is supported by at least one-fifth of a quorum, the vote shall be taken by electronic device.'
claims.sourceSpan: the vote shall be taken by electronic device unless the Speaker invokes another procedure for recording votes provided in this rule.
claims.note: Pass 1 finding (elision inside quotation marks). Draft's quote ended at 'electronic device.' with a period, but the source continues 'unless the Speaker invokes another procedure for recording votes provided in this rule.' Silent elision makes the electronic-device rule look absolute when it is a default subject to the Speaker's discretion. Extended the quote to include the full sentence.

claims.claim: Verbatim quote of Rule XX clause 2(a) 15-minute minimum for record vote or quorum call by electronic device

claims.section: Rule XX clause 4(a) â€” tellers-rule backup procedure
claims.note: Pass 1 finding (attribution error). The quoted span is verbatim in the source, but from clause 4(a) â€” the backup 'tellers' procedure the Speaker may direct when the electronic system is not used. The article's narrative sentence describes electronic-device voting, so the correct authority is clause 2(a): 'the minimum time for a record vote or quorum call by electronic device shall be 15 minutes.' Both minimums are 15 minutes, so the fact survived; the citation did not. Replaced with the clause 2(a) quote.

resolution: Pass 1 (hostile). Fixed 9 issues in the draft. Material: (1) intro's 'each chamber's own standing rules' â€” unsourced general civics framing; (2) intro's 'a few federal statutes' â€” overgeneralization (sources include one statute); (3) discharge's '218 Members' quote â€” misquote elided the inline citation and the 'not including Delegates or the Resident Commissioner' qualifier; (4) voting clause 1(b) quote â€” elision dropped 'unless the Speaker invokes another procedure...'; (5) voting's tellers-rule 15-minute quote used to support electronic-device voting narrative â€” clause 4(a) misattributed for what is clause 2(a); (6)/(7)/(8) Senate H2 answer made three claims about Senate procedure generally ('Almost all of it', 'Senate floor procedure lives in the Senate's own standing rules', 'The one place a federal statute expressly changes Senate debate') that require Senate-rules sources this hub does not carry. Minor: (9) discharge answer's 'eligible for a vote once a majority has signed it' collapsed the 7-legislative-day layover + call-up requirement into signing alone. All rewrites are source-anchored; no new claim, figure, or qualifier introduced.
